## You must change `src/`

This phase declares `must_touch: [src/]`. The gate fails the phase unless at
least one changed file falls under it. Writing tests, documentation or a report
is not enough — if you finish without touching that area, the phase fails on
exactly that check.

## The failure-assertion rule does not apply here

This phase declares `failure_assert: not_applicable`, so the gate does NOT
require a test asserting that a failure is produced. Your subsystem reports
problems as diagnostics or emits documents, so there is no `Result::Err` to
assert on. Every other test rule still applies in full.


## Evidence — verified finding

```
src/lexer.rs reserves 54 keyword words; 12 of them are never mentioned anywhere in src/parser.rs, so the lexer produces a token the parser has no rule for. Verified one by one against the built binary — every one exits 1 with `ParserError: Unexpected token <Kind>`: `when` (Unexpected token When), `ask` (Unexpected token Ask), `that` (Unexpected token That), `new` (Unexpected token New), `async` (Unexpected token Async), `wait` (Unexpected token Wait), `parallel` (Unexpected token Parallel), `done` (Unexpected token Done), `are` (Unexpected token Are). The other three (`until`, `might`/`fail`) are already owned by phase-040 and phase-038 and are NOT this phase's work. This is worse than a missing feature, because the word cannot be used as an identifier either: `set async to 1` fails the same way, so a perfectly ordinary variable name is rejected with a message that names an internal token kind the user has never heard of. SPEC.md documents four of these as working syntax — `async` at SPEC.md:906, `wait` at SPEC.md:915, `parallel`/`done` at SPEC.md:926-930, all under the heading `## Asynchronous Programming` — and docs/GRAMMAR.md:52 lists `'async' | 'wait' | 'parallel' | 'until'` in the reserved-word table with `async_function = 'async' function_decl` at :327 and `async_call = 'async' set_statement` at :328. SPEC.md's keyword appendix at :1020-1040 lists `when` (pattern matching), `this/that` (object reference), `new` (object instantiation), `is/are` (comparison or type checking) and `error` as language features. README.md:117-145 demonstrates none of them. The failure mode is the same signature defect phase-001 found with `Expr::Expect`: a token declared and never consumed.
```

**Re-verify this before you change anything.** If the finding no longer
reproduces on `main`, stop and write that to `FINDINGS.md` — a stale phase must
never be "fixed" by inventing a change.

## Goal

Decide per word — implement it, or free it so it can be an identifier — so no source file is rejected with a bare internal token name, and make SPEC.md, docs/GRAMMAR.md and the lexer agree.

## Method

1. Read `AGENTS.md` in full. Obey every hard rule; they are not negotiable.
2. Reproduce the finding. Record the exact command and the exact wrong output.
3. Write the failing test FIRST. Watch it fail. Do not touch production code
   until you have a red test that fails for the right reason.
4. Make the smallest change that turns it green.
5. Run the four gates yourself before claiming anything:

   ```bash
   cargo fmt --all -- --check
   cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
   cargo test --all-targets
   ./rbops/verify.sh phase-049
   ```

6. Write `REPORT.md` in the exact shape required by `AGENTS.md` section 4.

## Definition of done

- [ ] a test enumerates the lexer keyword table and the parser's token arms and FAILS on any word reserved by the lexer that no parser arm can consume — the enumeration itself is pasted into REPORT.md, so the list is not a one-off measurement
- [ ] every keyword left reserved is reachable: for each one, a .rb file using it parses and runs to exit 0, or the phase removes it from the lexer table and a test proves `set <word> to 1` then `say <word>` works
- [ ] for each of `async`, `wait`, `parallel`, `done`, `when`, `new`, `that`, `ask`, `are`: either it parses as the construct SPEC.md documents, or SPEC.md and docs/GRAMMAR.md are corrected and the correction is listed in REPORT.md — no word is left half-promised
- [ ] the three words owned elsewhere stay untouched: `until` (phase-040) and `might fail` (phase-038) are not implemented here and the test asserts they still fail the same way, so this phase cannot silently absorb or break them
- [ ] edge tests named edge_* cover: a reserved word used as a variable name, as a record field name, as a module name, and as a function parameter name — each either works or gives a spanned error whose message names the WORD and not an internal token kind
- [ ] the error message for a rejected program names the offending word, not `TokenKind::Async` — a test asserts the human-readable text
- [ ] `cargo test --all-targets` reports 0 failures, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean with no `allow(` added, and every file in examples/ and modules/ still exits 0
